comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 OER, checked 2026-09-25; the advertised 2027–28 revision is not substituted for this curriculum
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted OER lists two formal second-year tracks. Aardoppervlak is the first listed and is selected as neutral tie-break between equally substantial Earth-surface and Geologie en Geochemie routes, without reference to UCR. Year 1 is 60 compulsory EC; year 2 is 60 compulsory EC including the five Aardoppervlak-specific units; year 3 comprises 30 compulsory EC (Hydrology 6, Philosophy/History of Science 6, Bachelor thesis 18) and 30 genuinely open academic profiling/minor EC. Zero-credit language test and study/career component are not added. The VU advertises an overhauled programme from 2027–28, whose complete curriculum was not yet published; this record uses the adopted current 2026–27 OER.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The 2026–27 OER confirms two formal tracks; neither is uniquely representative of the broad Earth Sciences target. The first-listed Aardoppervlak track is chosen under the neutral order tie-break and its complete 60-EC second-year path is used. The choice was made without considering UCR fit.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Earth Science, mathematical and sustainability foundations precede Earth modelling, GIS, soils, resource analysis and upper-level biogeochemistry. All formal prerequisites and offered semesters were checked against the 2026 UCR workbook; advisory progression is sensible.

basisLabels: Earth-system processes, climate and landscape change

basisLabels: Earth-system processes, climate and landscape change
courseTraceability.rationale: Sustainability Essentials I examines planetary boundaries and physical environmental systems underpinning observed global change. It implements the explicit academic basis “Earth-system processes, climate and landscape change”.

basisLabels: Earth, life and climate over deep time
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Biodiversity studies the history and classification of life, including fossils and palaeontological evidence of changing biodiversity. It implements the explicit academic basis “Earth, life and climate over deep time”.

basisLabels: Earth-surface hazards and climate adaptation
courseTraceability.rationale: Natural Hazards, Risks & Adaptations examines earthquake, drought and climate-related geohazards using geoscience principles and risk evidence. It implements the explicit academic basis “Earth-surface hazards and climate adaptation”.

basisLabels: Earth-system processes, climate and landscape change

basisLabels: Geospatial, field, mathematical and statistical Earth-science methods

basisLabels: Earth-system processes, climate and landscape change

basisLabels: Earth-surface hazards and climate adaptation

basisLabels: Geospatial, field, mathematical and statistical Earth-science methods

basisLabels: Soils, water, biogeochemistry and subsurface resources

alternativeSelection.assessment: A second, geology-and-geochemistry-centered curriculum is supported by the formal route and direct interests, but UCR has only introductory deep-Earth work and limited near-surface geochemistry; it cannot supply a different credible 24-course deep geology and tectonics programme. Climate, water, geospatial data and subsurface resources are already substantively included in Alternative 1; no additional distinct direction survives the course and concept gates.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce the interacting spheres of the Earth; UCR gives an overview rather than the VU disciplinary sequence.
Both build models of coupled Earth-system processes, though the VU unit belongs to a geological major.
Both address global environmental and climatic change; UCR emphasizes contemporary climate impacts.
Both examine the formation and transformation of landscapes; UCR focuses on coastal and delta settings.

notes.text: The VU Earth Sciences route includes substantial geology, geomorphology, field mapping and an 18-EC individual Earth-science thesis. UCR offers Earth-system, soil, water, climate and geospatial work, but not the same sequence of geological fieldwork or specialist Earth-science depth; its delta research course is a group applied project.
